Yes. The subtext enriches the story rather than feeling forced. The looping corridors and indistinguishable infants make Nora’s disorientation physical while suggesting her uncertainty about motherhood and the expectation of instant recognition and love.

The exchange of looks in the lobby also carries an unspoken possibility of mutual recognition without confirming what the other woman knows. Finally, Nora’s repeated promise to “call tomorrow” exposes the tension between her genuine attachment and her avoidance of responsibility. These implications emerge naturally through setting, gestures, and hesitation, giving the story emotional and moral complexity.
